canonical_rules.representative_verbatim: Hybrid BPNST with neurofibromatous and schwannomatous differentiation (hybrid neurofibroma/schwannoma) as in our second case has also been described. Feany et al. reported the largest series of hybrid neurofibroma/schwannoma, including a total of 9 tumors arising in 9 patients. These tumors were reported to arise sometimes in the setting of a neurofibromatosis 1 (NF1) or schwannomatosis, but are not confined to this type of patients, as they were also reported in patients with no stigmata for these syndromes [8, 9]. The cases reported by Feany et al. were described to arise in dermal, subcutaneous, or subfascial areas. They often showed a predominance of neurofibromatous loose myxoid areas in plexiform arrangement, delimited at the periphery by a perineurium and including in their center a well-defined nodule of a schwannomatous differentiation. Interestingly, plexiform neurofibromas are considered pathognomonic for NF1; however, in our case and in 5 out of the 9 patients with hybrid plexiform neurofibroma including schwannomatous nodules reported by Feany et al., the clinical examination failed to demonstrate stigmata of neurofibromatosis. In this report, one patient with nonplexiform hybrid tumors was diagnosed with NF1. Mitoses were rarely found in the schwannomatous component but not in the neurofibromatous one. Recurrence was reported in only 1 out of the 9 cases reported by Feany et al., and it occurred 44 years after the initial excision.

findings.claim: Hybrid perineurioma-schwannoma -> well circumscribed but unencapsulated
findings.verbatim_support: Hornick et al. discribed 42 cases of benign nerve sheath tumors showing hybrid features of perineurioma and schwannoma as in our first example. These tumors appeared to be architecturally typical of soft-tissue perineurioma, being well circumscribed but unen- capsulated and showing storiform to whorled and lamellar growth patterns. findings.verbatim_support: Hybrid BPNST with neurofibromatous and schwannomatous differentiation (hybrid neurofibroma/schwannoma) as in our second case has also been described. Feany et al. reported the largest series of hybrid neurofibroma/schwannoma, including a total of 9 tumors arising in 9 patients. These tumors were reported to arise sometimes in the setting of a neurofibromatosis 1 (NF1) or schwannomatosis, but are not confined to this type of patients, as they were also reported in patients with no stigmata for these syndromes [8, 9]. map_chunks.summary_text: This chunk describes hybrid benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors (hybrid BPNST) with combined neurofibromatous and schwannomatous differentiation [S1|PMC5803675_dpa-0004-0001|9409]. The largest reported series (Feany et al.) comprised 9 tumors in 9 patients [S2|PMC5803675_dpa-0004-0001|9409]. These tumors arise in the setting of NF1 or schwannomatosis but also occur in patients without any syndrome stigmata [S3|PMC5803675_dpa-0004-0001|9409]. Anatomically, tumors arose in dermal, subcutaneous, or subfascial locations [S4|PMC5803675_dpa-0004-0001|9409]. Histologically, they characteristically show plexiform neurofibromatous loose myxoid areas delimited by perineurium, with a central well-defined schwannomatous nodule [S5|PMC5803675_dpa-0004-0001|9409]. Notably, 5 of 9 patients with hybrid plexiform neurofibroma/schwannoma lacked NF1 stigmata despite plexiform neurofibromas being classically pathognomonic for NF1 [S6|PMC5803675_dpa-0004-0001|9409], while one patient with nonplexiform hybrid tumor did have NF1 [S7|PMC5803675_dpa-0004-0001|9409]. Mitoses were rarely seen in the schwannomatous component and absent in the neurofibromatous component [S8|PMC5803675_dpa-0004-0001|9409]. Recurrence was uncommon, occurring in only 1/9 cases and 44 years after initial excision [S9|PMC5803675_dpa-0004-0001|9409].

findings.claim: Hybrid BPNST -> differential diagnosis includes other BPNST and low-grade MPNST
findings.verbatim_support: The main differential diagnosis for hybrid BPNST includes other BPNST and low-grade malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNST). The composite nature of these lesions could be easily overlooked if only limited immunohistochemistry is performed (for example only S100 protein or EMA). As nuclear atypia could be seen in the hybrid tumors, a low-grade MPNST might be considered. However, MPNST show variation in cellularity and a mitotic activity that is generally either very low or absent in hybrid BPNST. The atypia seen in hybrid tumors are of a degenerative nature similar to that seen in other benign nerve sheath tumors (i.e., smudged chromatin, nuclear pseudoinclusions).

map_chunks.summary_text: This chunk addresses the differential diagnosis of hybrid benign peripheral nerve sheath tumors (BPNST). The primary differentials include other BPNSTs and low-grade malignant peripheral nerve sheath tumors (MPNST) [S1|PMC5803675_dpa-0004-0001|9410]. The composite nature of hybrid BPNST can be missed when only limited IHC markers (e.g., S100 protein or EMA alone) are used [S2|PMC5803675_dpa-0004-0001|9410]. Nuclear atypia is present in hybrid BPNST and may raise concern for low-grade MPNST [S3|PMC5803675_dpa-0004-0001|9410]; however, MPNST is distinguished by variation in cellularity, whereas mitotic activity is generally very low or absent in hybrid BPNST [S4|PMC5803675_dpa-0004-0001|9410]. Importantly, the atypia in hybrid BPNST is degenerative in character—manifesting as smudged chromatin and nuclear pseudoinclusions—analogous to that seen in other benign nerve sheath tumors [S5|PMC5803675_dpa-0004-0001|9410].
